title: Classic Beef Carpaccio with Rocket, Cherry Tomatoes and Mustard-Lemon Sauce
summary: Paper-thin rounds of raw beef fillet with a peppery rocket salad, quartered cherry tomatoes and a creamy mustard-lemon sauce drizzled over the top.
equipment: rolling pin or flat meat mallet

ingredients.item: beef fillet (tenderloin), centre cut, one very fresh whole piece
ingredients.note: trimmed of all fat and silver skin

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Chill the fillet hard
steps.text: Roll the fillet tightly in cling film and freeze for 45-60 min, until the outside is firm but the centre still gives a little. That stiffness is what makes very thin slicing possible.

steps.title: Slice across the grain
steps.text: Using your sharpest thin blade, cut 3 mm slices across the grain. Cutting this way shortens the muscle fibres, so every mouthful is tender.

steps.title: Flatten the slices
steps.text: Sandwich a few slices at a time between baking paper and roll or tap them gently until 1-2 mm thick and nearly translucent. Lay them slightly overlapping so they cover each chilled plate, and return the plates to the fridge.

steps.title: Blend the sauce
steps.text: Put 4 tbsp olive oil, the lemon juice, mustard, egg yolk, a pinch of salt and some pepper into the tall jug. Blitz with the stick blender for 20-30 s; the yolk and mustard emulsify the oil into a thick, pale yellow sauce.

steps.title: Dress the rocket
steps.text: Just before serving, toss the leaves with 1 tbsp oil and a pinch each of salt and pepper. Dressing late keeps them from wilting.

steps.title: Plate and serve
steps.text: Pile the rocket in the centre of each plate and trail the sauce in a circle across the beef. Dot over the tomato quarters, season the meat with the last of the salt and pepper and eat within a few minutes, while the beef is still cold.

tips: RAW NOTE: the beef is eaten raw. Use a very fresh whole-muscle piece from a butcher you trust, trim and slice it yourself just before serving (never pre-minced beef), and keep it below 4 °C until it goes on the plate. Pregnant people, young children, older adults and anyone with weakened immunity should skip it.

EGG NOTE: the yolk in the sauce is raw. Use a pasteurised egg yolk; pregnant people, young children, older adults and anyone with weakened immunity should use a sauce of just oil, lemon and mustard instead.
A common mistake is slicing the beef straight from the fridge; it is too soft and tears, so give it the full time in the freezer first.
Chill the plates for at least 15 minutes so the thin beef stays cold right up to the table.
If the sauce is too thick to drizzle, blend in 1-2 tsp cold water.
storage: Serve carpaccio as soon as it is plated and discard any leftovers. The sauce keeps for up to 1 day covered in the fridge. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
